A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ScaleZero and Dynamic Parameter Scaling (DPS) research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original online reinforcement-learning results on Atari, DMC, and Jericho, including architectural ablations, gradient analyses, and DPS efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and additionally reports DPS parameter-dynamics analyses and a preliminary frozen-DINOv2 encoder comparison.

M1.justification: The core ScaleZero architecture and staged DPS strategy remain. However, v3 Section 4.3 and Algorithm 2 introduce a trainable base-model scale, fix the currently trained adapter's scale at 1, and optimize earlier adapters' scales. Appendix A.4 also introduces bounded scalar reparameterization, refining the update procedure specified in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Atari26 suite, Atari8 ablation subset, DMC18 tasks, and four Jericho games. Joint training across all three domains remains future work in v3; the added analyses do not establish new task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1a adds UniZero (MT) to the Atari26 comparison, which previously contained only UniZero (ST) and ScaleZero (MT). Appendix A.2.2 newly reports comparing a frozen DINOv2 encoder against the existing from-scratch ViT. The DMC and Jericho comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: Appendix B.1 replaces four stacked grayscale Atari frames with one RGB frame; DMC training/inference context lengths change from 10/4 to 5/2, with revised discount and replay-buffer settings. DPS Table 6 changes five expansion stages to five total stages, including warm-up. These are substantive reporting revisions, but the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.4 and Figures 11–12 analyze DPS stage transitions, solved-task progress, and adapter scales across layers and attention components, substantially extending the investigation of DPS mechanisms. Appendix A.2.2 adds a qualitative pretrained-encoder comparison. Existing plasticity, routing, and gradient-conflict analyses are retained, including the complete analysis corresponding to v1's removed main-text Figure 4.

E5.justification: DMC's reported seed count changes from three in v1 Appendix C.1/Figure 10 to two in v3 Appendix C.1/Figure 9. Both retain 95% confidence-interval reporting, and Jericho remains at two seeds. This establishes changed reporting, not when or whether runs were repeated.

E6.justification: Central DPS efficiency results are revised: v1's prose reports approximately 20% savings while Figure 5 labels 40.5%; v3's prose and revised Figure 4 both report 28.5%. This is not an established same-setting improvement. v3 also adds UniZero (MT) Atari scores of 0.31 mean/0.16 median, quantitative DPS dynamics, resource comparisons, and approximately 40% MoCo training overhead. Existing ScaleZero benchmark summary scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The MoE assumptions, Theorems E.1–E.3, Corollary E.4, and their proofs are retained. A limited mathematical change occurs in DPS: v3 Equations 7–8 redefine the effective weight using a base-model coefficient and bounded tanh-parameterized scales, replacing v1's unscaled base and unrestricted scalar formulation.

C1.justification: The principal contributions—diagnosing plasticity collapse, proposing ScaleZero, and allocating capacity through DPS—remain. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion revise the headline efficiency claim from approximately 80% to 71.5% of interactions, with the introduction explicitly tying the revised saving to DMC.

C2.justification: v3 adds hierarchical and functional explanations of DPS adapter behavior, a domain-gap explanation for DINOv2's lack of consistent gains, and a gradient-norm-collapse hypothesis in Appendix B.2.2. Appendix G expands the existing limitations discussion with untested joint-domain training, limited coordination between MoE and LoRA, and online-learning cold-start constraints.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands implementation documentation with UniZero planning/loss details, distributed MoCo pseudocode, task partitioning and gradient accumulation, benchmark-specific hyperparameters, and active/total parameter accounting. Hardware and training-time reports are revised, including Jericho from eight A100s/about one day to four A100s/about three days. Conversely, v1's explicit dormant-neuron threshold of 0.025 is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 substantially develops DPS's positioning against static offline LoRA adaptation and adds a detailed rationale for excluding model-free and offline comparators in Appendix A.8. It connects the plasticity argument to newer sparsity research and adds works including LoRAHub and DINOv2, while removing discussions/references including LoRAMoE, QLoRA, and DoRA. These changes exceed relocation or bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, method exposition, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before the background with an extended appendix treatment; implementation sections are reorganized and expanded. v3 also adds an appendix contents page, separate limitations, ethics/reproducibility statements, acknowledgements, and a language-model-use disclosure.

P2.justification: v3 combines the Atari and DMC summaries into Table 1, adds architecture/configuration/resource tables and DPS diagnostic figures, and expands the Jericho trajectory display from two games to four. Schematics, legends, colors, captions, and theory takeaway boxes are revised. The redundant main-text plasticity figure disappears while its data remain in the complete appendix figure.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability through the direct multitask baseline, fuller implementation/resource documentation, and DPS diagnostics. It also resolves v1's conflicting textual and plotted efficiency savings by consistently reporting 28.5%. These benefits are limited by unresolved inconsistencies: Table 11 says Jericho has no MoE layers, contradicting Appendix A.5's description. The revision provides a modest net gain in clarity and support, without establishing broad new performance improvements.
